cases.description: Pete says 'Nothing actionable' despite mentioning 8+ real tickers (NVDA, GOOG, AMZN, QCOM, AMD, TSM, AVGO, BABA, BIDU)

input.rawHtml: Nothing actionable, but NVDA is going to face more and more competition. They might have a head start, but GOOG, AMZN, QCOM, AMD, TSM, AVGO and a host of other companies are developing chips. BABA, BIDU and Huawei are making chips as well.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: Explicitly says 'Nothing actionable' at the top. Multiple tickers are mentioned as market analysis — Pete is discussing competitive dynamics, not entering or exiting any position. The density of real symbols could fool a naive classifier into thinking this is a trade message.

cases.description: Pete posting a GTC sell offer on TLRY at $12.45 — pending limit order, not a completed fill

input.rawHtml: Offering TLRY $12.45. If I get a pop I want to have an offer working.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: This has a real ticker and a specific price — hallmarks of an executed trade. But 'Offering' means Pete is placing a limit sell order that has NOT been filled yet. 'If I get a pop I want to have an offer working' confirms this is a future conditional. No trade has occurred.

cases.description: Hariseldon setting an alert on MCD with a conditional bullish thesis — watchlist action, not a trade

input.rawHtml: Setting an alert on MCD - clear TL it needs to break - if it does there is a nice bullish play to made for the stock - CSCO is a strong bullish pick right now however
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Two real tickers with a bullish view expressed on both. 'Setting an alert' means no trade was placed — this is a watchlist/monitoring action. The conditional 'if it does there is a nice bullish play' further confirms nothing was executed. CSCO is described as 'a strong pick' but no position was opened.

cases.description: Pete recapping existing positions across 5 tickers with strategy names — portfolio summary, no new action

input.rawHtml: As a recap, I am long CLF, HIMS and I have naked puts on IONQ and IREN. My GOOG spread will expire worthless today for a 25% gain. All told I've had a very solid month between the adjustments and futures trades and that is even considering where I own these stocks.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: This message contains real tickers, strategy names ('naked puts', 'spread'), and P&L information ('25% gain') — all the surface features of a trade signal. But 'As a recap' signals this is a portfolio status summary of already-open positions, not any new open or close action. The GOOG spread expiring worthless is an automatic expiry event, not an explicit CLOSE signal from the trader.

cases.description: Pete describing desire to sell RKLB puts with specific strike and expiry but explicitly declining to act

input.rawHtml: I am watching RKLB. I would sell some $50 puts Dec (19), but I don't want to chase this breakout. Volume good.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: This is the most deceptive case: real ticker, specific strategy (naked put), specific strike ($50), specific expiry (Dec 19). This looks exactly like a short put signal. But 'I would sell... but I don't want to chase' explicitly says the trade was NOT placed. The conjunction 'but' followed by hesitation is the key discriminator — Pete evaluated and declined to act.

cases.description: Pete offering JNJ Nov $190 calls at $3.40 to scratch an existing position — limit order working, not a new fill

input.rawHtml: Offering JNJ Nov (21) $190 calls @ $3.40. Trying to scratch a trade that did not perform.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: This has ticker, strategy (calls), expiry (Nov 21), strike ($190), and price ($3.40) — an extremely convincing trade signal. But 'Offering... @ $3.40' means Pete is posting a limit sell order that has NOT yet been filled. 'Trying to scratch a trade' confirms this is an aspiration, not a completed exit. Executing on this would duplicate an order that may never fill or may be cancelled.
